title: Document
description: One profile: its settings and a tree of items, each placed by the engine and drawn from its scene. Format infopanel.document/1; see docs/document.md. View state (selection, expansion, zoom) is never part of a document.

requires.description: Document capabilities beyond version 1.0. An engine that lacks one doesn't open the document for editing (see docs/versioning.md).

rev.description: The document's revision: it goes up with every change (edits, undo, redo, revert).

items.description: Top-level items in drawing order: the first is at the back.

rev.description: The document revision at which a profile field last changed.

background.description: Every frame starts as this colour; a transparent one lets a desktop window show what is behind it.

statsOverlay.description: Draw the engine's frame-rate overlay on every output.

locale.description: The regional format numbers and dates are drawn in (see docs/expressions.md, Regional format). Absent: the PC's regional format.

triggerApps.description: Applications (process names) whose being in front should bring this profile up. Stored; acted on by engines that support it.

guides.description: Editor-only guide lines: saved with the document and undone like any edit, never drawn on any output.

editor.description: Client data kept with the document (for example defaults for new items); opaque to the engine. At most 64 KiB.

windowSettings.description: The profile's desktop window (one per profile), shown at one frame pixel per pixel of the display it is on, up to the 16,777,216-pixel frame cap, above which the frame is drawn smaller and stretched over the window (docs/document.md).

enabled.description: Show the profile in a desktop window.

x.description: Pixels from the left of the matched display.

y.description: Pixels from the top of the matched display.

strict.description: Hide the window when no display matches `display` exactly.

displayMatch.description: The display the window belongs on, matched by name and size in the display's pixels; x and y, in the desktop's own coordinates, tell displays of the same name and size apart. No exact match: hidden when strict, else the first display with the name, else the first with the size, else the main one. Absent: the main display (docs/document.md).

width.description: The display's width in its own pixels.

height.description: The display's height in its own pixels.

x.description: The display's left edge in the desktop's own coordinates (points on macOS, not pixels on a scaled display).

y.description: The display's top edge in the desktop's own coordinates (points on macOS, not pixels on a scaled display).

guide.description: A guide line across the whole canvas: axis x is a vertical line at x = at, axis y a horizontal one at y = at.

sceneItem.description: An item that draws a scene, placed by `placement` in its parent's coordinates.

locked.description: Editors don't move or change a locked item; the engine doesn't enforce it.

groupItem.description: An item that holds other items. Its children are placed in its coordinates: the group's placement moves and rotates them as one.

visible.description: false hides the group and everything in it.

children.description: In drawing order: the first is at the back.

itemRev.description: The document revision at which the item last changed. Ignored when a client inserts an item.

itemName.description: A name for people (layer lists); not shown on outputs.

placement.description: Where the engine puts the item: its local origin (0, 0) at (x, y) in the parent's coordinates, rotated clockwise by `rotation` degrees about `pivot` (local coordinates). See docs/geometry.md.

pivot.description: Absent: half the layout box's size on each axis where it is set, 0 where it is automatic (and (0, 0) for groups).

layout.description: The item's layout box, (0, 0)–(w, h) in local coordinates; the scene reads it with {"op": "box"}. An absent dimension is automatic: the content decides it. A client that changes it usually sends a new scene too (setDesign).

bindings.description: The sensor each scene input reads, by input name. Bindings for names the scene doesn't declare are kept and ignored.

key.description: A sensor key as the engine lists them (GET /api/sensors).

source.description: How the client produced the scene, so it can produce it again. Opaque to the engine apart from this envelope: `format` names the client's own description in `data`; or `ref` is an opaque reference the engine never interprets, with the description kept elsewhere. `deps` lists stored blobs the description needs; the engine keeps them while any retained version of the document refers to them.

sourceDeps.description: The stored blobs the description needs, each once. They have no count of their own: `sourceBytes` bounds them (docs/limits.md).

origin.description: Where the item came from, recorded by the client; opaque to the engine, kept on copy. At most 4 KiB.
